property_summary: After calling assertGovernanceApproved, configured is always true when the first transferFrom succeeds and the unlock time condition is not met.
After a call to assertGovernanceApproved that does not revert, configured must be true.
After calling assertGovernanceApproved where the transferFrom succeeds and the pending unlock time is less than block.timestamp, configured remains true.
After any call to assertGovernanceApproved that does not revert, configured must be true.
After any call to assertGovernanceApproved, configured remains true.
After calling assertGovernanceApproved, the DAO address should remain different from address(0).
After calling assertGovernanceApproved, the DAO address equals the initial deployment address (this contract).
After calling assertGovernanceApproved, the DAO address remains the initial deployment address.
After a call to assertGovernanceApproved, the DAO address must remain the address set by the constructor (the test contract itself).
The DAO address must always equal the address passed in the constructor (this) unless a successful proposal changes it.
After a call to assertGovernanceApproved, reading DAO returns the address of the contract that deployed C (the original argument to setDAO) if the call succeeded, not address(this).
After calling setDAO with any address, DAO always equals the input address.
After calling assertGovernanceApproved with any parameters, the value of DAO remains unchanged from before the call.
After any call to setDAO, the final value of DAO equals the argument passed to setDAO.
When assertGovernanceApproved is called by a non-DAO address that is governed, the transaction reverts because the flash governance asset transfer fails, so DAO remains unchanged.
After calling assertGovernanceApproved with any parameters, the stored governance config (amount, asset, unlockTime) is unchanged from before the call.
After any call to assertGovernanceApproved, the DAO address stays the same as before the call.
After assertGovernanceApproved, the `governed` status of the caller's target address is the same as the boolean passed to setGoverned for that address.
After any sequence of calls ending with assertGovernanceApproved, the governed status of each address in the last setGoverned call equals the corresponding isGoverned value.

After any sequence of calls ending with assertGovernanceApproved, the governed status of each address in the most recent setGoverned call equals the corresponding isGoverned value, provided the setGoverned call succeeded.

After any sequence of calls ending with a call to assertGovernanceApproved, the caller is governed exactly if it was the DAO or if it was set as governed in the most recent successful setGoverned call.
After any successful call to setGoverned, the mapping governed[addr] for each addr in the call must equal the isGoverned value passed for that addr.
After assertGovernanceApproved is called by an address, that address becomes governed (governed[caller] is true).
After assertGovernanceApproved is called by a non-DAO address, the mapping `governed` remains unchanged for all addresses.
After a successful governance decision, the governed status of any address that was previously set via setGoverned remains as set.
After any sequence of calls ending with assertGovernanceApproved, the governed mapping value for any address that was not previously set via setGoverned remains at its default false.
After any call to assertGovernanceApproved, the governed mapping of any address that was previously explicitly set via setGoverned remains unchanged.
After calling assertGovernanceApproved, pendingFlashDecision[target][sender].unlockTime must be >= block.timestamp (i.e., the unlockTime is set to current timestamp plus the configured unlockTime).
After assertGovernanceApproved, pendingFlashDecision[target][sender].asset equals flashGovernanceConfig.asset
After assertGovernanceApproved, if the transfer was successful, pendingFlashDecision[target][sender].unlockTime must be strictly positive.
If assertGovernanceApproved succeeds (does not revert), then pendingFlashDecision[target][sender].unlockTime must be greater than block.timestamp at the time of the call.
After a successful call to assertGovernanceApproved, the unlockTime stored for that (target, sender) pair must equal block.timestamp + the configured flashGovernanceConfig.unlockTime.
After any call to assertGovernanceApproved, the value of security.lastFlashGovernanceAct equals the current block timestamp.
After a successful non-emergency assertGovernanceApproved call, the security.lastFlashGovernanceAct value increments by at least the block timestamp difference between consecutive calls.
After a successful non-emergency call to assertGovernanceApproved, security.lastFlashGovernanceAct must be equal to the current block timestamp.
After a successful non-emergency call to assertGovernanceApproved, the value of lastFlashGovernanceAct must be updated to the current block timestamp.

When assertGovernanceApproved completes successfully in non-emergency mode, security.lastFlashGovernanceAct must be greater than or equal to the maximum of the previous lastFlashGovernanceAct and the block timestamp at the start of the call.
When emergency is true, the call to assertGovernanceApproved should succeed regardless of epoch timing; in P it does, in M it may revert if the epoch check fails.
When emergency is true, assertGovernanceApproved succeeds if the transfer succeeds and pending timestamp check passes, regardless of the epoch timing.
When emergency is true, assertGovernanceApproved always succeeds if the token transfer and pending unlock check pass, regardless of epoch timing.
When emergency is true, assertGovernanceApproved always reverts in M but succeeds in P if token transfer and pending unlock check pass.
When emergency is true, the call to assertGovernanceApproved should succeed if the token transfer and pending unlock timestamp check pass.
